long_biography.plain_text:
At 24, Wypychewicz left a state-sector electrical job to open a workshop in his father-in-law's garage. He competed through practical invention, faster delivery and persistent direct selling. The installation business grew into ZPUE, adding factories and acquiring other electrical-engineering operations before joining the Warsaw Stock Exchange in 1999.

The group later expanded from transformer stations and switchgear into energy storage and electric-vehicle charging infrastructure. After its 2022 delisting, the family consolidated ownership and structured its assets through Koronea. Wypychewicz now serves as a non-executive director of the family office and deputy chair of ZPUE's supervisory board, while the next generation manages daily operations.
